lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is Carhenge — on September 30, both HARC and Town Council hold special meetings dedicated entirely to the proposed redevelopment at 700 W. Pacific Avenue, with HARC reviewing preliminary architecture for all building clusters and Council taking up a subdivision appeal that could determine whether the project moves forward at all. The county is also workshopping a proposed Employee Housing Impact Fee that could reshape how growth gets paid for across San Miguel County. Elsewhere, the town spends three hours shaping the 2027 General Fund budget, and the Original Thinkers festival and San Miguel River Cleanup round out a genuinely full week.

notable.stake: HARC reviews preliminary architecture for all Carhenge building clusters at 700 W. Pacific.
Council decides a subdivision appeal that could block or greenlight the entire Carhenge redevelopment.
Commissioners workshop a new Employee Housing Impact Fee for unincorporated San Miguel County.
Final architecture review for 15 employee apartments and 4 new multifamily units in Mountain Village.
Town sketches 2027 General Fund priorities, revenue, fees, and capital spending before formal adoption.
